clips.send: Radio waves. longer than 30 cm. Radio waves pass through clouds and even work in daytime, so radio telescopes can observe in any weather. Radio waves are so long that a dish must be enormous to see sharp detail. China’s FAST is 500 m (1,640 ft) across, the size of 30 soccer fields. Several dishes far apart can be linked to act like one giant telescope. In 2019, eight observatories linked across the whole Earth took the first picture of a black hole. Radio equals longest waves, lowest energy, biggest dishes.

clips.send: Gamma rays. shorter than 0.01 nm. The most energetic light there is: one gamma-ray photon can carry millions of times the energy of a visible-light photon. Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them completely, which protects life on the ground. Space telescopes like NASA’s Fermi catch them directly. Ground telescopes can only see the faint blue flash a very high-energy gamma ray makes when it smashes into the upper air. Gamma equals the most energetic. Shortest wave, highest energy.

clips.send: X-rays. 0.01 – 10 nm. X-ray telescopes show the hottest places in the universe, from millions to hundreds of millions of degrees. X-rays would go straight into a normal mirror, so telescopes like Chandra use nested, barrel-shaped mirrors that X-rays skim off at a very low angle, like a stone skipping on water. Our atmosphere stops all of them, so X-ray astronomy only became possible with rockets and satellites. X-rays, extreme heat (millions of degrees).

clips.send: Infrared. 700 nm – 1 mm. Infrared (IR) passes through dust that blocks visible light, so it shows baby stars hidden inside dark clouds. Light from the most distant galaxies has been stretched by the expanding universe from visible into infrared. That is why JWST is an infrared telescope. Water vapour in our air absorbs most infrared. Only a few “windows” get through, best from high, dry mountains. JWST has to be kept colder than minus 230 degrees Celsius so its own warmth doesn’t drown out the faint signals. Infrared equals “below red”: you feel it as warmth from a campfire.

clips.send: Visible light. 400 – 700 nm. The only light your eyes can detect: violet ( about 400 nm) through blue, green, yellow and orange to red ( about 700 nm). It is a tiny sliver of the whole spectrum, much less than one millionth of the range on this slider, but it is where the Sun gives off the most light. It passes through clear air, which is why telescopes have been built on the ground for 400 years. ROY G BIV: red has the longest visible wave, violet the shortest.

clips.send: Ultraviolet. 10 – 400 nm. Ultraviolet (UV) light comes from things hotter than the Sun’s surface, such as young blue stars. The ozone layer absorbs almost all UV shorter than about 300 nm. A little of the longer UV gets through: that is what gives you a sunburn. Hubble can see in ultraviolet because it orbits above the atmosphere. UV equals “beyond violet”: just past the violet end of the rainbow.

clips.send: Microwaves. 1 mm – 30 cm. Every direction in the sky glows faintly in microwaves: it is the cosmic microwave background, light left over from about 380,000 years after the Big Bang. ALMA, 66 dishes on a 5,000 m (16,400 ft) high plateau in Chile, uses millimeter waves to see planets forming around young stars. Microwaves are often counted as short radio waves. Your microwave oven uses 12 cm waves; your Wi-Fi uses 6 or 12 cm. Microwaves: from the Big Bang’s afterglow to your kitchen.

clips.send: 无线电波（射电）。长于 30 厘米。无线电波能穿过云层，白天也能观测，所以射电望远镜在什么天气都能工作。无线电波很长，天线必须非常大才能看清细节。中国的 FAST（“中国天眼”）直径 500 米（1640 英尺），大约有 30 个足球场那么大。把相距很远的几面天线连在一起，就像一台巨大的望远镜。2019 年，遍布全球的 8 个天文台联合拍出了第一张黑洞照片。无线电波：波最长，能量最低，天线最大。

clips.send: 伽马射线。短于 0.01 纳米。能量最高的光：一个伽马射线光子携带的能量可以是可见光光子的几百万倍。地球大气把它们完全吸收了，这保护了地面上的生命。像 NASA 的费米这样的太空望远镜能直接接收它们。地面望远镜只能看到极高能伽马射线撞进高层大气时产生的微弱蓝光。伽马射线能量最高：波长最短，能量最大。

clips.send: X 射线。0.01 – 10 纳米。X 射线望远镜能看到宇宙中最热的地方，从几百万度到几亿度。X 射线会直接钻进普通镜子里，所以钱德拉这样的望远镜用一层套一层的桶形镜面，让 X 射线以很小的角度“擦”过去，就像打水漂的石子。大气把 X 射线全部挡住了，所以只有有了火箭和卫星以后，才可能进行 X 射线天文观测。X 射线，极高温（几百万度）。

clips.send: 可见光。400 – 700 纳米。这是你的眼睛唯一能感知的光：从紫色（约 400 纳米）到蓝、绿、黄、橙，再到红色（约 700 纳米）。它只占整个电磁波谱的一小条，不到这个滑块范围的百万分之一，却正是太阳发光最多的波段。它能穿过晴朗的空气，所以 400 年来人们一直在地面上建望远镜。红橙黄绿蓝靛紫：红光的波长最长，紫光最短。

clips.send: 红外线。700 纳米 – 1 毫米。红外线能穿过挡住可见光的尘埃，所以能看到藏在暗云里的“婴儿恒星”。宇宙在膨胀，最遥远星系发出的光已经从可见光被拉长成了红外线。这就是 JWST 是一台红外望远镜的原因。空气中的水汽吸收了大部分红外线，只有几个“窗口”能透过来，在又高又干燥的山顶上效果最好。JWST 必须保持在零下 230 摄氏度 以下，才不会被自身的热量淹没那些微弱的信号。红外线 等于 “红色之下”：你在篝火旁感到的温暖就是它。

clips.send: 微波。1 毫米 – 30 厘米。天空的每一个方向都发出微弱的微波，这就是宇宙微波背景辐射：大爆炸后约 38 万年留下来的光。ALMA 由 66 面天线组成，建在智利海拔 5000 米（16,400 英尺）的高原上，用毫米波观测年轻恒星周围正在形成的行星。微波常常被算作较短的无线电波。微波炉用的是 12 厘米的波，Wi-Fi 用 6 或 12 厘米的波。微波：从大爆炸的余晖到你家厨房。

clips.send: 紫外线。10 – 400 纳米。紫外线来自比太阳表面更热的东西，比如年轻的蓝色恒星。臭氧层吸收了几乎所有波长短于约 300 纳米的紫外线。波长较长的紫外线有一小部分能穿过来，这就是让你晒伤的光。哈勃望远镜在大气层之上运行，所以能拍紫外线照片。紫外线 等于 “紫色之外”：就在彩虹紫色那一端的外面。
